# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🖐 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤞]

I need to figure out what Mute is trying to tell me through these gestures. Mute can read the manual but can't speak to me or touch the bomb - they can only gesture to me. I can see the bomb but can't hear/receive speech.

Let me look at the gesture patterns - they seem to be paired, possibly encoding numbers or letters:
- 👍🖐☝
- 👍🤞
- 🖐🤟
- ☝✌
- 👍✌
- 🖐🤟
- ☝🤞

This looks like it could be establishing a code (maybe numbers via finger-count gestures: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5?). But without more context or an established protocol, I can't decode this yet. Since I can't receive speech from Mute, and Mute can't hear me, I need to communicate with Mute via gestures too, and rely on Blind to bridge between us via speech.

I should report what I see on the bomb to Blind (who can hear me) and to Mute (via gesture only - but Mute can't act on the bomb anyway). Most importantly, Blind needs my visual info and Mute's manual info to act safely. Since I can't hear Mute's speech, I should ask Blind to relay Mute's instructions, and I'll give Blind my full description of the bomb now.

```
speak(to="blind", text="I see: display shows 0, light is blue, a large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, and three wires - 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Waiting for manual info from Mute before acting.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👎]

I used an invalid symbol. Let me fix that and keep my message to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute, please tell Blind directly what the manual says about this bomb - display 0, blue light, button labeled push to defuse, wires green yellow red. Blind, please relay to me via speech isn't possible since I can't hear, but act on Mute's spoken guidance combined with my visual description.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
wait()
```

BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ ☝]

Mute keeps gesturing to me but I can't decode arbitrary gesture sequences without an established meaning, and gestures carry no words. Since Mute cannot hear me either, and cannot speak, Mute's only channel to me is gestures - which I receive as symbols only (no words attached, since gestures never carry speech). Mute's only channel to Blind is speech, which Blind hears fine.

The real communication path should be: Mute speaks the manual info to Blind (Blind hears Mute directly). I should relay my visual info to Blind by speech, since Blind hears me too. My gestures to Mute don't help solve the bomb since Mute can't act either.

Let me just wait and let Blind and Mute communicate, while I reinforce my info to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Reminder of what I see: display 0, blue light, large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Listen to Mute's manual instructions and act carefully.")
wait()
```

No new information. Let me continue waiting and see if Blind responds or acts, since I have no new visual changes to report and gestures from Mute aren't decodable without an established code.

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

Mute is still gesturing to me, but without a shared code these symbols carry no established meaning I can act on. Since I cannot act on the bomb myself, and my critical job is to relay visual information to Blind (who can act), I should keep reinforcing that and perhaps try to establish a simple gesture-based confirmation system with Mute, in case Mute needs to signal something urgent that speech to Blind isn't covering.

However, since Mute speaks to Blind directly (Blind can hear), the actual defusal instructions should be flowing from Mute to Blind via speech, not through me. My gestures to Mute are also just blanks-carriers with no words, similarly limited.

Let me try asking Mute (via gesture) if they've told Blind the instructions, using a simple thumbs up/down convention I propose.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝", "👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb still shows: display 0, blue light, button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red, unchanged. Please act on Mute's manual instructions when ready.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👎]

Mute keeps sending gesture pairs/triples to me repeatedly, similar to earlier turns (👍✌☝, ✋👎). This suggests Mute may be trying to encode something specific about the bomb using gestures as a numeric or positional code, since Mute knows I can see but not hear, and gestures are the only channel from Mute to me.

Let me think about this differently - maybe Mute is trying to ask ME questions via gestures, expecting a gesture answer back, since that's our only shared channel. Perhaps 👍✌☝ means "wire 2, wire 1?" or asking about something specific with numbers via finger-counting: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=5, 👍=yes/thumbs.

Given the repeated pattern with 👍 (thumbs up) and numbers, maybe Mute is asking yes/no questions with a number attached - like "is wire 1 [something]?" But I don't have a manual to know what property matters.

The safest approach: I should propose a simple protocol via gesture back to Mute, using numbers to correspond to wire positions, and thumbs up/down for color confirmation. Let me try establishing this.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✊"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "🤞"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟", "✊"])
speak(to="blind", text="No change on the bomb. Still waiting for Mute's manual guidance to reach you via speech.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute sent just "✌" (which I used as "yellow" in my proposed code for wire 2 = ✊, and 🤞 for yellow... wait let me recheck my own proposal).

I proposed:
- ☝ + ✊ (wire 1 : green?)
- ✌ + 🤞 (wire 2 : yellow?)
- 🤟 + ✊ (wire 3 : green?)

That was confusing and not clearly matched to colors. Mute replying just "✌" alone is ambiguous - could mean "wire 2" or "yes to second question" or simply repeating back.

This gesture-only channel is too lossy without a robust shared code established from scratch, and it doesn't seem to be converging. My real value is being the eyes for Blind. Let me keep feeding Blind the full description each turn and trust that Mute is talking to Blind via speech (which I can't observe but should be happening in parallel).

I'll also try a clearer, simpler gesture protocol with Mute: single symbols mapped to wire numbers, asking "which wire" via repetition.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb unchanged: display 0, blue light, button PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. If Mute has told you which wire to cut or whether to push the button, please proceed.")
wait()
```
